html:
SMTO-SCH-0027 — The schedule the Agent chose didn't match your request

GUID: 40038ddd-6412-4198-9bc8-4aa12486ddd4
Slug: temporal-schedule-mismatch
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The Agent tried to create a schedule with a different time, or a different kind of schedule, than you asked for. SMTO stopped it before anything was saved and told the Agent what you asked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open. The Agent normally creates the schedule again with the time from your message. SMTO gives the Agent the timing and kind of schedule from your message so it can correct itself.
  2. Open Schedules and check that only one schedule for this request exists, with the Next run you meant. This confirms the right time was saved and no extra copy was made.
  3. If you want a different time, send a new message with the exact date, time and time zone. SMTO only changes the time you asked for when you tell it to.

What success looks like

  • One schedule for your request appears on the Schedules page with the time you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing rejected schedule.create because its timing fields differ from the captured deferred timing, combine a relative interval with next_run_at, or fail the anchored absolute-time check.

What this means

  • Proposed schedule fields differ from expected captured timing, combine a relative interval with overriding next_run_at, or fail the anchored absolute-time comparison. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Proposed schedule fields differ from expected captured timing, combine a relative interval with overriding next_run_at, or fail the anchored absolute-time comparison.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare expected route fields and absolute clock/timezone facts before accepting any timing change.

How to fix it

  • temporal_routing.guard (phase pending_schedule) rejected schedule.create because its action_type, schedule_type or interval_seconds differ from expected(route), because next_run_at was sent alongside a captured relative interval, or because an absolute_once next_run_at is unparsable or not later than the captured clock's now in its timezone. The model should resend schedule.create with the fields in the correction's expected object; ask the user before changing the intended timing.
  • Use the expected captured schedule fields and supported recurrence representation. Ask for clarification before changing the user’s intended timing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported schedule fields reproduce the intended captured timing exactly.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
